free_tier.stated: no free tier; Windows - Plus is EUR 16.99 a month for 8 vCores, 16 GB of RAM and 250 GB, quoted with tax included, and the yearly cycle takes 16.7 per cent off

retention.stated: the disk persists while the plan is paid; the page states no deletion clock

egress.terms: not stated on the plan lines read: the page prints price, vCores, RAM and disk for each plan and no traffic volume, port speed or overage price

interface_detail: Windows is installed at checkout at no extra charge and the admin path is RDP on the issued address; the vendor states it neither supplies nor resells the Microsoft licence
tooling: any RDP client; no API or console is described on the plan page read
chaining: the cheapest 8 vCore, 16 GB row whose licence position is stated plainly rather than left blank, and the statement is bring-your-own. It pairs with a licence channel at about USD 14.17 a month, which puts the honest all-in figure near USD 33.21 rather than 19.02.
limits_note: the page prints four cycles: monthly, quarterly, half-yearly and yearly, where quarterly and half-yearly are the monthly price multiplied with no discount and only the yearly payment applies -16.7 per cent. The 20 per cent VAT rate appears in the vendor's own worked example rather than as a line on the plan. No byte quota, port speed, request rate or object cap is printed, which is why limits[] is empty rather than padded with a kind the vocabulary does not cover.
binding_note: nothing in the seven-kind vocabulary binds, because the vendor publishes no quota of any kind. The constraint that decides the row is commercial rather than a limit: Windows installs at no charge but the key is the buyer's, and a licence channel costs more per month than the machine.

identity_cost.detail: an account and a payment method at order

reliability_note: no reliability event observed; the yearly discount is illustrated on the entry plan and the figure for Plus is arithmetic on the stated percentage rather than a printed total.
confidence_note: the plan, its shape, the EUR 16.99 tax-inclusive price, the four cycles and the bring-your-own-licence sentence are read from the vendor page on 2026-10-26. Two derived numbers are weaker and labelled as arithmetic: the yearly equivalent of EUR 15.84 a month and the USD conversion at 1.1193. The 20 per cent VAT rate is the vendor's own example, not a printed line on this plan.

evidence.proved: quoted: 'Windows - Plus EUR 16.99/mo (8 vCores, 16 GB, 250 GB)', beside 'Windows - Core EUR 9.99/mo (4 vCores, 8 GB, 100 GB)' and 'Windows - Max EUR 28.99/mo (16 vCores, 32 GB, 500 GB)'

quoted on the licence: 'the Microsoft licence is not included: we install the system you choose at checkout at no extra charge, but we neither supply nor resell a licence'; the string BYOL does not occur and this sentence is the bring-your-own…
quoted on cycles: 'Monthly, quarterly, half-yearly and yearly. Quarterly and half-yearly are simply the monthly price multiplied, with no discount: only yearly payment applies -16.7%'
quoted on tax: 'our prices are shown with tax included' and the worked example 'An ex-VAT price of EUR 6.99 comes to EUR 8.39 including VAT', which is a 20 per cent rate applied by the vendor itself

notes: The EUR 16.99 is tax-inclusive, so it is not comparable with an ex-VAT figure without adjusting, and the USD 19.02 conversion inherits that basis. The yearly figure is EUR 14.15 a month equivalent, or USD 15.84, and the yearly invoice is EUR 169.83, which is USD 190.09 at 1.1193; the vendor illustrates the 16.7 per cent discount on its entry plan rather than on Plus, so the Plus figure is arithmetic on a printed percentage. The licence gate is the honest caveat: at USD 14.17 a month for a 16-core Standard licence channel the all-in cost is near USD 33.21, which is roughly what a licence-printed row costs.

extras.term: none monthly; yearly at 16.7 per cent off
extras.windows_licence: bring your own: installed at checkout at no charge, licence neither supplied nor resold
extras.windows_images: buyer's choice at checkout, named per order rather than listed on the page
